blocks.html:
If you were going to tell a friend about eating in Maha Sarakham, you'd start with what this city actually is. Maha Sarakham is the Taksila city — Isan's education hub, with Mahasarakham University and Rajabhat at its core. A university city means the food is cheap and varied in a way that other provinces rarely match. Running through the Tha Khon Yang zone in front of MSU you'll find Isan restaurants, jaew hawn shops, riverside spots, and new cafés lined up in a row. Come further into the old city behind the old campus and you'll find hand-made noodle shops that have been quietly excellent for decades. Evening comes with a cool breeze, the smell of charcoal-grilled chicken drifting over, a hot jaew hawn pot circling the table — that's the atmosphere people carry home with them from Maha Sarakham.

This list covers the restaurants the whole city talks about: Suanahan Tong Grilled Chicken, famous for crispy-skin chicken with its house-formula jaew sauce; Kuayjab Boran Mae Oi behind the old campus, rolling its own fresh noodles every single day until the hand-cut strands are thicker and chewier than anything you'd find in a factory pack. For genuine Isan flavours there's Lam Chi 1 opposite Big C, known for koi seua kua and soi ju; and Krua Chaipharuay near the Wang Yao junction, making tom pla chon and crispy laab pla tapian in a style that's getting harder to find. Café people have She's Cafe & Bistro by the Chi River and homey spots like Miso Home Cafe and Brotherhood near MSU. Every restaurant on this list has been endorsed by people from Maha Sarakham. Work through them one by one and you'll understand why this small city punches above its weight on food.

blocks.name: Suanahan Tong Grilled Chicken (Suanahan Tong Kai Yang)
blocks.area: Mueang Maha Sarakham District, Maha Sarakham
blocks.signature: Crispy-skin grilled chicken with house-formula jaew dipping sauce, laab catfish, upiae
blocks.descHtml:
Ask a Maha Sarakham local which grilled chicken restaurant is legendary and many will bring you to Suanahan Tong Grilled Chicken. This shaded wooden pavilion in the Waeng Nang sub-district, on the road toward the new provincial hall near Nong Ya Plong area, has been open for over 30 years — making it one of the first names people in Sarakham reach for when they want serious Isan food and grilled chicken. Perfect for a first meal in the province, coming as a family or group, since there are garden pavilions, communal tables, and air-conditioned function rooms seating hundreds.

The star is the herbal-marinated grilled chicken, which comes out with genuinely crispy skin, tender meat, not dry or tough. Reviews consistently say: "skin extra crispy, flavour deep." Dipped in the restaurant's house jaew sauce and paired with fragrant sticky rice wrapped in banana leaf, it's a solid combination. Beyond the chicken there's laab catfish, upiae (a local-style braised offal dish), and Thai and Lao-style som tum, made with the seasoning intensity of real Isan cooking. Anyone who wants heat orders som tum alongside the chicken.

Pricing is very accessible — roughly 101–250 THB per head, the main grilled chicken dish around 140 THB. Good value for the quantity and quality. Vintage-styled décor, clean and open, comfortable at both lunchtime and in the evening. Open daily 09:30–18:00 (delivery available via GrabFood, LINE MAN, foodpanda). Note the restaurant closes relatively early, so a lunch or mid-afternoon visit works best. Holiday weekends get busy — a provincial landmark draws a crowd. Come for a set of grilled chicken and som tum together, then add laab catfish or upiae to taste. A proper Isan meal, just as people say you have to stop here when you come to Sarakham.
mustOrder: Crispy-skin grilled chicken with house jaew sauce
blocks.bestFor: First meal in the province — families and groups

blocks.name: Jaew Hawn (Tha Khon Yang)
blocks.signature: Wagyu beef jaew hawn with rich herb broth, grilled pork neck, crispy seafood som tum
blocks.descHtml:
Ask a Maha Sarakham local what to take an out-of-town friend to eat, and Jaew Hawn Tha Khon Yang comes up near the top. This restaurant has been running for over forty years since 1984, growing into a large garden restaurant on Thinannont Road in front of Mahasarakham University. Perfect for anyone who wants original-style jaew hawn in a shaded, comfortable setting — families, groups of friends, or a social dinner where sitting long is the point.

The star is the Wagyu beef jaew hawn set — a pot of rich herb broth that reviewers consistently praise for its clear herbal fragrance, round balance, and warmth in the stomach. Dipped into the restaurant's house jaew sauce, the flavour is even better. Fresh Wagyu comes thinly sliced to cook in the pot yourself, tender and just right. For grill lovers, the fragrant pork neck is essential, and the crispy seafood som tum hits with proper intensity. A local favourite that regulars order every time is the pla lui suan — fresh fish with an abundance of herb condiments.

Prices run roughly 101–250 THB per head. The jaew hawn set starts around 220–260 THB; snacks start in the low hundreds. Good value for a long, leisurely meal. Open daily around 10:00–23:00, with outdoor seating under trees, several air-conditioned rooms seating hundreds, live music, and ample parking. Easy to reach since it's right on the main road.

The popularity is well-earned. The restaurant has won the LINE MAN Wongnai Users' Choice award for multiple consecutive years and was selected as a provincial heritage dish by the Ministry of Culture. Worth knowing: busy evenings on weekends mean large tables should call ahead, and the broth runs quite spicy-hot — ask staff to adjust if needed.
mustOrder: Wagyu beef jaew hawn set with rich herb broth
blocks.bestFor: Family meal or group social dinner — long sitting style
blocks.zone: Tha Khon Yang (in front of MSU)

blocks.name: Yor Phu Thai Tha Khon Yang
blocks.area: Tha Khon Yang, Kantharawichai District, Maha Sarakham
blocks.signature: Concentrated om hwai (rattan stew), pla nin lui suan, jaew hawn, honey grass jelly
blocks.descHtml:
Yor Phu Thai Tha Khon Yang is a long-established Isan garden restaurant in the new MSU zone, serving the Tha Khon Yang community for over seventeen years. It sits next to Chai Phupha fresh market, opposite Krung Thai Bank Tha Khon Yang branch — easy to find on the main road. Perfect for students, families, and groups of friends looking for a relaxed table from midday well into the evening. For visitors coming to Maha Sarakham who want to try genuine local home-style cooking, this is a spot locals like to bring people to.

The dishes that keep selling out are om hwai — intensely concentrated, herbaceous and rounded — and pla nin lui suan: tilapia topped with a generous, punchy herb dressing. For people who want something hot and brothy, there's jaew hawn with a herb-rich broth starting at around 189 THB, great to eat with side dishes and take your time over. Finish with cold honey grass jelly to cool down. Reviews broadly agree: large portions, real Isan intensity, good value — though some note that on busy days waiting times can stretch.

The atmosphere is a strong selling point. One side is a shaded garden restaurant with fans at every table; inside there's a floating raft platform over the water, a private, pleasant spot by day or night. In the evening, live folk music adds to the mood. A second section of the restaurant runs a 99 THB muu kratha buffet in the evenings for people who want all-you-can-eat. Staff earn consistent praise for attentive service.

Average spend around 101–250 THB per head — very reasonable for a meal that comes with both food and atmosphere. Parking available, cards accepted, free Wi-Fi. Open from morning to midnight. Worth knowing: evenings on holidays get quite full; if you're in a group or want the water raft seating, arriving early secures the best spots.
blocks.bestFor: Evening social dinner with friends or family

blocks.name: Kuayjab Boran Mae Oi (Behind the Old Campus)
blocks.signature: Fresh hand-rolled kuayjab noodles — wide, chewy strands — with pork meatballs, moo yor, and blood cakes
blocks.descHtml:
If you were recommending a dish that Maha Sarakham people are proud of, Kuayjab Boran Mae Oi behind the old campus would always make the list. The restaurant has been here for decades, and what keeps people talking is one thing: hand-rolled fresh kuayjab noodles, made daily. Using a blend of rice flour and tapioca flour, kneaded in-house and rolled into sheets, then cut thicker and wider than standard kuayjab noodles. Dozens of kilograms rolled fresh every day, never overnight — which means every bowl you get has noodles that grip your teeth with a chew that's genuinely hard to find. This is the spot for anyone who wants kuayjab with real character, not factory strands.

The order to make is the classic kuayjab boran bowl, which arrives loaded with pork meatballs (moo deng), moo yor sausage, good-sized blood cake, and offal packed into the bowl. Anyone wanting more can order the special extra-loaded version. A runner-up dish that regulars keep adding is braised chicken carcass in broth, cooked until the bones are soft and good to gnaw — great as an extra. The flavour across reviews reads as: clear, well-balanced broth with roasted chilli for depth, and the noodles are the hero — chewy-firm in a way that makes people say eating them elsewhere is never the same.

The atmosphere is simple, unpretentious local, warm in a home-kitchen way. Nothing fancy, but comfortable and easy. Prices are very low — around 50 THB per bowl, portions packed. Location on the new-cut road behind the old campus within Mueang district. Roadside parking in front. Open daily 06:00–22:00 — breakfast, lunch, or late night, all viable.

This restaurant's popularity isn't trend-driven — it's consistent hand-rolled noodles and broth that never slips. Sarakham locals bring people here repeatedly; out-of-towners usually get a tip to visit. One thing to note: there are other Mae Oi locations around the city — if you want this branch specifically, use the coordinates for "behind the old campus, new-cut road." During peak hours, bowls are cooked to order one at a time, so a brief wait is normal.
mustOrder: Classic fresh kuayjab (moo deng, moo yor, blood cake)
blocks.bestFor: Morning or late-night — hand-rolled noodle lovers

blocks.name: Yaowarat
blocks.signature: Fresh hand-made egg noodles, tom yum noodles, red pork and crispy pork, rice with braised soft-bone pork in red sauce
blocks.descHtml:
Yaowarat is a Chinese-style noodle and made-to-order restaurant in the city centre of Maha Sarakham, tucked into a lane in the middle of the Sri Sawat Damnoeng Road area near the old city market. Perfect for anyone who wants fresh-made egg noodles in the authentic Yaowarat style in an air-conditioned, comfortable space. The thing every review agrees on is that the egg noodles are made in-house — kneaded and rolled by the restaurant — coming out as thin, firm, springy strands that don't absorb too much flour and don't dissolve in the bowl. If you're a noodle person, this is worth the trip.

The must-order is the tom yum noodle soup — thick, sharp, punchy broth with red pork, crispy wontons, and morning glory. Another item regulars keep coming back for is the dry egg noodles with crispy pork, where the pork comes with genuinely crispy skin over tender meat, and the rice with braised soft-bone pork in red sauce, cooked until the bones are meltingly soft. Beyond these, there are also fresh spring rolls, pork-knuckle spring rolls, red pork and crispy pork rice, dim sum, Chinese-style fish cake, and fish maw soup — plenty of sides and extras. Customers consistently praise the red pork as genuinely good and all the portions as generous and well-presented.

Prices are very friendly — most noodle bowls around 40–45 THB, rice dishes well under 100 THB per head, snacks starting in the low tens. Clean shop, parking available, multiple staff so food comes out fast. Ideal for a quick weekday lunch or a casual drop-in meal.

Strong consistent ratings reflect ongoing popularity. The restaurant regularly ranks near the top of the city and has a loyal regular crowd every Friday–Saturday. Worth noting: closed Wednesdays. Busy periods mean a short queue — coming before noon or in the mid-afternoon makes for a smoother visit.
mustOrder: Dry egg noodles with crispy pork
Rice with braised soft-bone pork in red sauce
blocks.bestFor: Quick weekday lunch — fresh egg noodle lovers

blocks.name: She's Cafe & Bistro
blocks.area: Tha Khon Yang Sub-district, Kantharawichai District, Maha Sarakham
blocks.signature: Multi-style riverside food and seafood, cakes and cheesecakes, flamingo-by-the-river photo spot
blocks.descHtml:
She's Cafe & Bistro is a restaurant on the Chi River in Tha Khon Yang, Kantharawichai District, known for wide river views and a relaxed atmosphere that works for a whole evening — sunset through to late night. Good for couples who want a quiet drink by the water, or groups and families celebrating a birthday or anniversary. The space is divided into multiple zones: a glass-walled air-conditioned bar section, an open upper floor with full river views, a breeze-cooled terrace garden, and private sofa-dome pods. The flamingo-pink river corner that photographs well is the spot most people mention.

The menu spans a lot: Thai food, old-style Thai, Chinese, Italian fusion, and a full seafood spread. Dishes that come up regularly in reviews include crispy catfish salad, battered squid, pineapple rice, German-style pork knuckle, and seafood like large scallops, grilled river prawns, oysters, and cheese-baked lobster. For the café crowd, there's a good selection of cakes — blueberry cheesecake, New York cheesecake, strawberry shortcake — paired with coffee, lemonade, green tea, or hot chocolate.

Reviews generally say the food is genuinely good and the atmosphere delivers, especially in the evening when the light falls over the water. At night, live music lifts the mood further. Prices roughly 101–250 THB per head for a regular meal, climbing for seafood orders or larger tables. Wine and imported beers available; credit cards accepted (with surcharge).

Open daily from mid-afternoon through to midnight. Worth knowing: parking in front of the restaurant is limited — many people park at the nearby temple but check closing times. The restaurant sits down a road next to the water, so using maps navigation is helpful. For an evening river table on weekends, calling ahead to reserve is worth it, as the best-view spots go quickly.
blocks.bestFor: Riverside dinner watching the sunset — long sitting with a group

blocks.name: Lam Chi 1
blocks.area: Mueang Maha Sarakham District (opposite Big C Maha Sarakham), Maha Sarakham
blocks.signature: Koi seua kua, soi ju, laab and koi, grilled beef, jaew hawn
blocks.descHtml:
Ask a Maha Sarakham local where to go for laab and koi at 3 a.m. and Lam Chi 1 comes up immediately — because it has been part of the city for decades, it sits directly opposite Big C Maha Sarakham so it's very easy to find, and crucially it's open 24 hours. Any meal, any time of night or day, there are people eating. Good for meat lovers who want fresh-sourced Isan food in the real local style, groups of friends, or families — large, well-ventilated space with plenty of tables, both open and air-conditioned, with a parking lot.

The dish almost every table orders is koi seua kua — raw beef sliced fresh — and soi ju, dipped into hot jaew dipping sauce. Then laab, koi, grilled beef, and a jaew hawn pot to gather around as a group. For people who want more variety, there's tom khom, pla 3 rot, or gaeng som chom goong to add. The main selling point consistently praised in reviews is freshness — the restaurant selects its meat fresh for the purpose. For raw-beef and koi fans, this is the right place.

Prices are accessible — main dishes starting around 60–80 THB per dish; a full table meal per head roughly 101–250 THB. Google rating 4.3 from over 600 reviews reflects a customer base that keeps returning. The popularity comes from the easy-to-find location, never closing, and the long-established fresh-meat laab koi style that has become part of the Sarakham eating identity. Visitors seeking real Isan food regularly stop here.

One honest note: the restaurant's flavour leans toward genuine home-style Isan — straightforward and real. Some reviews mention that a few items like sun-dried beef can occasionally run dry. Best to focus on the koi, soi ju, and fresh beef dishes where the kitchen is at its strongest. Ask for more chilli if you like heat. Coming as a group and ordering jaew hawn to share around the table is the most satisfying way to experience Lam Chi 1.

blocks.name: Miso Home Cafe
blocks.area: Waeng Nang Sub-district, Mueang Maha Sarakham District, Maha Sarakham
blocks.signature: Korean-style drinks, macarons, bakery in a homey café atmosphere
blocks.descHtml:
If you want the feel of Korea without a long flight, Miso Home Cafe is a small café in the owner's residential compound that many people call the most authentically Korean café in Maha Sarakham — because the owner is Korean. From the name and menu signage to the décor, the Korean atmosphere is woven in seamlessly. The building is a large white house, decorated in clean white tones with marble details and wood accents, nearly all glass walls for plenty of natural light. Every angle photographs well. Perfect for the café-and-photo crowd, and anyone who wants a quiet corner to sit.

The most-talked-about item is the macaron — the restaurant's signature — with a large shell, generous filling, sweetness balanced without being cloying. Korean-style drinks and strawberry milk have earned consistent good reviews. For coffee people, the iced americano here uses imported beans, brewed unsweetened, full aroma and bitterness intact. There's also a selection of bakery to pair with drinks — a one-stop for both sweets and coffee.

Prices are relaxed: most drinks and snacks well under 100 THB per item (around 50–80 THB), the americano at roughly 80 THB — good value for the quality and the atmosphere. Located at Ban Non Duea, Moo 10, Waeng Nang Sub-district, Mueang Maha Sarakham, about 3 kilometres from the city centre toward Kaeng Leng Jan. Open approximately 10:00–18:00.

Highly popular among young people and MSU students for combining genuine Korean ownership, a photogenic space, and food that delivers. Worth noting: the café sometimes closes on certain Wednesdays and opening times can shift slightly — checking the page or Instagram before visiting is advisable. Parking available in the compound. Weekends can get busy.

blocks.name: Brotherhood : Bake House & Cafe
blocks.signature: Homemade cakes and pastries, daifuku, coffee in a warm, wood-toned homey café
blocks.descHtml:
If you're an MSU student or have ever passed through Maha Sarakham near the university gate, the name Brotherhood : Bake House & Cafe is probably familiar. This café has been part of the neighbourhood for many years and many student generations. A warm, brown-toned homey café that feels like visiting a friend's house — the building is covered in climbing vines for shade outside, with an outdoor garden zone and a cool air-conditioned room that several regulars say gets beautiful light, especially around late afternoon when the sun comes in at just the right angle. Good for working, reading, and anyone who likes a quiet, personal atmosphere.

The star here is the homemade cakes and pastries, made in-house. Items mentioned often in reviews: fresh-milk strawberry cake, fresh butter bread, and daifuku — which many people describe as a must-try, with a soft, pillowy texture and sweetness that's perfectly calibrated. Drinks are well-made too; the lychee rose soda has a delicate floral freshness. Coffee people have several choices. Come alone to work with coffee, or come as a group and share a selection of cakes — both work equally well.

Prices are university-neighbourhood friendly — most items roughly 100–200 THB per head. Google rating 4.4 stars. Points people consistently bring up: shaded and photogenic, varied seating options, and power outlets for those sitting long.

Location is in the lane opposite Kalpapruek condo on the MSU gate road (faculty side), Kham Riang Sub-district, Kantharawichai. Open daily 10:30–20:00. It's a small lane in the university zone — maps navigation helps. Evenings on weekends get busy; coming before mid-afternoon catches the best light and a more relaxed atmosphere.
blocks.bestFor: Working or reading alone — near MSU

blocks.name: Krua Chaipharuay
blocks.area: Mueang Maha Sarakham District, Maha Sarakham
blocks.signature: Lao-style tom pla chon, crispy laab pla tapian, laab puu na (field crab laab), som tum with local vegetables
blocks.descHtml:
Closing the list at Krua Chaipharuay — a home-style restaurant that makes Sarakham locals and passing travellers alike turn in. It sits along Highway 213 near the Wang Yao junction in Koeng Sub-district, Mueang District — a short drive from the city centre. The defining quality of this place is that it's a genuine local Thai home-kitchen (Thai baan) that makes you feel like you've gone back to visit your grandmother in the middle of a rice field. Waterside pavilions, green field views, vintage-style décor. Good for whole families, a group of friends who want to sit and breathe in the breeze, or anyone who misses Isan home cooking that's getting rarer every year.

The dish almost every table orders is the Lao-style tom pla chon — a hot, punchy, well-rounded broth — and crispy laab pla tapian: snakehead-pattern fish fried until the skin is genuinely crispy while the inside stays moist, not oil-heavy. Another speciality that's hard to find elsewhere is laab puu na (field crab laab), served with a generous pile of local herbs, a clear herbaceous fragrance. The som tum with local vegetables uses the restaurant's own pla ra sauce, and both fried pla som and garlic-fried tender fish are praised in genuine reviews for that crispy-outside soft-inside quality, good even to eat the whole head.

People who visit agree: fresh ingredients, clean vegetables, no off-smells, because the restaurant sources from local gardens around the area. Flavours are bold and right — genuine Isan intensity. Friendly staff who point you toward the menu. Service fast. Prices comfortable at roughly 101–250 THB per head; large portions, good value. Wongnai rating 4.6 reflects a customer base that comes back because the flavour doesn't change.

Worth knowing before you go: the restaurant is open during the day through the early evening, roughly 09:30–17:30, and closed every Monday. A lunch or mid-afternoon sitting with river breeze is the ideal time. Call ahead or arrive before noon on weekends to get a good spot.
blocks.bestFor: Riverside lunch with family — relaxed sitting

blocks.title: Know before you eat in Maha Sarakham

items.title: Getting around the city
items.text: Maha Sarakham is a small city — most restaurants are either in the city centre or in the Tha Khon Yang zone in front of MSU. Grab has a limited fleet here; renting a motorbike or driving yourself is the easiest option. Most restaurants are only a few minutes apart.

items.title: Bring cash
items.text: Noodle shops, street stalls, and small Isan restaurants often accept cash only or PromptPay. ATMs are available around the city, but having small notes on hand saves time.

items.title: Avoid the crowded windows
items.text: Friday–Saturday evenings and during MSU term time, popular restaurants in the Tha Khon Yang zone get packed. If you don't want to wait, try the mid-afternoon window or before 18:00. Some noodle shops sell out by mid-afternoon.

items.title: You can specify your spice level
items.text: Isan dishes like laab, koi, som tum, and soi ju are genuinely spicy. If you can't handle heat, tell the restaurant you want less spice or no chilli. Som tum without chilli is a normal request.

items.title: English menus are limited
items.text: Most local restaurants have Thai-only menus. Cafés and riverside restaurants have some English. Using food photos on your phone or a translation app to point at items works fine. People here are friendly and helpful with visitors.

items.title: Tipping
items.text: Local and street restaurants don't expect tips — pay the bill as shown. At sit-down restaurants with table service, rounding up or leaving a small amount is fine but not obligatory.

blocks.title: Plan your Maha Sarakham eating in 1–2 days
blocks.html:
If you have one day, here's a schedule that works well. Lunch: start at Kuayjab Boran Mae Oi behind the old campus — hand-rolled noodles at 35–55 THB per bowl — or Yaowarat in the old city quarter with fresh-made egg noodles. Order the tom yum noodles and rice with braised soft-bone pork together. Mid-afternoon, step into a café for a break: Miso Home Cafe in Waeng Nang toward Kaeng Leng Jan, or Brotherhood near the MSU gate with homemade cakes and daifuku.

For dinner, go big. If you're with a group, Jaew Hawn Tha Khon Yang or Suanahan Tong Grilled Chicken — order crispy chicken at around 140 THB per bird with laab, koi, and som tum to share. Very good value. For proper laab and koi, Lam Chi 1 opposite Big C is the address — koi seua kua and soi ju at 60–80 THB per dish. If you want a riverside close-out, head to She's Cafe & Bistro in Tha Khon Yang. Most of these restaurants are not far from each other — a short drive or a Grab ride connects them.

faq.q: Which Maha Sarakham restaurant is the most famous?
faq.a: By review scores, Krua Chaipharuay near the Wang Yao junction leads with a rating around 4.6, known for Lao-style tom pla chon and crispy laab pla tapian. Kuayjab Boran Mae Oi behind the old campus follows closely (around 4.5) for its hand-rolled noodles. For grilled chicken and jaew hawn, Suanahan Tong Grilled Chicken and Jaew Hawn Tha Khon Yang are the names the whole city talks about.

faq.q: What are the signature foods of Maha Sarakham that you have to try?
faq.a: Isan food is the hero here. Crispy grilled chicken with jaew dipping sauce, laab, koi, soi ju, and Wagyu beef jaew hawn with rich herb broth are the must-orders. Another signature of the Taksila city is hand-made noodles: fresh-rolled kuayjab from Mae Oi and fresh egg noodles from Yaowarat. For something unusual, try koi seua kua at Lam Chi 1.

faq.q: How much does eating in Maha Sarakham cost?
faq.a: Very affordable because it's a university city. Noodle shops like Kuayjab Mae Oi are 35–55 THB per bowl; Yaowarat egg noodles 40–80 THB per dish; laab and koi at Lam Chi 1 around 60–80 THB per dish. Sit-down Isan restaurants like Tong Grilled Chicken, Jaew Hawn, or Krua Chaipharuay run roughly 101–250 THB per head; grilled chicken around 140 THB per bird. Café drinks 50–80 THB per item.

faq.q: Do Maha Sarakham restaurants require advance bookings?
faq.a: Most are walk-in — just turn up. But popular sit-down restaurants like Jaew Hawn Tha Khon Yang, Suanahan Tong Grilled Chicken, or She's Cafe & Bistro riverside get busy on Friday–Saturday evenings and during MSU term time. Large groups should call ahead. Noodle shops and cafés are always walk-in.

faq.q: Are Maha Sarakham restaurants open in the evening through to late night?
faq.a: Yes, there are options for any hour. Noodle shops like Kuayjab Mae Oi and Yaowarat focus on daytime through mid-afternoon. Sit-down Isan restaurants like Tong Grilled Chicken, Jaew Hawn Tha Khon Yang, Lam Chi 1, and Krua Chaipharuay are open into the evening — good for a long dinner with friends. Check individual opening times in the map before heading out, as some restaurants close on specific days.
